Hi Devon — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide an ops-level proof-of-path diagram and a subprocessor roster specific to the EU-anchored deployment. For transient syncs we limit them to a single-hop (EU -> EU failover or EU -> EU edge) in the normal configuration; temporary out-of-region windows are only allowed under documented and auditable conditions (controlled by the customer pin policy).

I attached a concise overview (redwood_region_affinity_overview.pdf) and a draft DPA addendum for region-pinning (DPA_addendum_region_pin.docx). High level:
- Proof-of-path: we provide a network + control-plane diagram showing primary EU placement, KV cache affinity, and how prefetched tokens are handled via ephemeral edge caches. We can also produce a sanitized log extract showing VPC egress events for a short sample window.
- Transient sync: default policy is 0 outbound egress from EU to other regions. Exceptions: (a) authorized on-call ops-triggered failover (documented, 90m max window by policy), (b) customer-approved temporary crosshop for migration with a signed ticket (window negotiated case-by-case). When exceptions occur we (i) notify customers, (ii) record a signed ticket, and (iii) rotate ephemeral keys.
- Subprocessors: the roster for EU-anchored instances is limited to EU-region cloud infra (provider compute), our telemetry aggregator (still EU-hosted for pinned customers) and a limited CDN/edge provider that may operate in the broader EMEA region. We do not include US analytics in the roster for pinned customers unless explicitly enabled.

Next steps: Marissa will follow up with the ops-level diagram and a proposed sanitized log extract. Karthik will confirm the subprocessor roster and the language for the addendum (he's our lead on DPA edits).

Can you confirm whether CardioHealth needs the full unsanitized logs (we usually provide sanitized samples but can coordinate a more detailed evidence transfer under an NDA or in-person review)?

Best,

Tessa Morgan

Hi Devon — looping in the ops artifacts you requested. Attached is the region affinity overview (same PDF Tessa attached) and a short runbook excerpt that shows the failover path and the audit fields we populate when a transient sync is initiated.

Quick clarifications (ops-level):
- Normal operations: all tenant compute & KV replicas for EU-pinned customers are placed in eu-central-1 and eu-west-1 (active/standby) with strict routing; no egress to non-EU regions.
- Transient sync events: we treat these as change-of-state with required justification and a TTL. The policy enforces a 90-minute maximum window for temporary outbound hops; in practice our median transient sync is < 8 minutes for cache priming during rolling upgrades.
- Single-hop guarantee: any transient outbound path (rare) is configured as a single outbound hop to a pre-authorized site; we do not cascade across regions.
- Subprocessor visibility: we maintain a scoped roster per customer. For CardioHealth's EU pin we list: (1) ProviderComputeEU (IaaS - eu-central), (2) EdgeCDN-EMEA (edge caching), (3) TelemetryEU (metrics/alerts). None of these services transfer copies to US analytics unless you request analytics export.

Attachments: redwood_region_affinity_overview.pdf, DPA_addendum_region_pin.docx

If helpful, we can produce a short sanitized log bundle (TLS metadata only + egress event markers) for an afternoon window next week. Let us know whether CardioHealth legal prefers the sanitized bundle or an in-person review under NDA.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

1) Evidence scope: CardioHealth legal prefers an in-person review of unsanitized logs under our mutual NDA. Can Redwood commit to a 1-week window to make logs available at your Bellevue office (or neutral location) next month?

If you can confirm the availability for an in-person review and whether you accept the 30-minute escalation threshold language, we can route the addendum through our legal queue. Thanks again — we like your guarded approach and the single-hop guarantee.
